title: Union of Lublin
summary: In 1569 the Polish-Lithuanian union became a real parliamentary one, joining the two states under a common ruler and parliament. Lithuania sought equal noble rights and help against Moscow. The union created a regional power, the strongest in Eastern and Central Europe until the mid-seventeenth century.
